attacks.claim: The embargo badge text is hardcoded white on a surface that is white in the default light theme, so the embargo label is invisible (1:1 contrast). The hardcoded color also bypasses the theme tokens, so it fails in light mode even though the amber outline renders.
attacks.evidence: .embargo { ... background: var(--surface); color: #ffffff; } with tokens.css setting --surface: #ffffff for :root (light is default)

attacks.claim: The unpublish control is a <span> with only a mouse onClick. It is not focusable, has no role, no keyboard handler, no focus-visible style, and no accessible name, so keyboard-only and screen-reader editors cannot unpublish. This violates WCAG 2.1.1 and 4.1.2 in a release-gated app.

The unpublish action is rendered for every published draft and the client performs no role check. The artifact does not show that the server authorizes unpublish, so any user who can see the queue may be able to pull public stories.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no authorization check or permission gate for unpublish in DraftRow.tsx or the PR description; the button renders for any row where draft.status === "published"

attacks.claim: Unpublishing removes a live story from the public site with no stated audit record, cache/CDN purge, or handling for copies already syndicated or sent to wires. The rollback is a manual republish, and the artifact does not describe any record of who pulled the story or when.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: audit logging, cache invalidation, or syndication handling; body text only says "will be removed from the site and returned to drafts"

attacks.claim: onUnpublish is awaited with no try/catch, error state, or loading or disabled state. If the request fails, the editor gets no feedback and the row still shows as published. A repeated click during the request can also trigger a second call.
The PR says unpublish is 'one-click', but the confirm dialog makes it a two-step action. The stated value claim is inaccurate relative to the implementation.
attacks.evidence: "a one-click unpublish action on each queue row" vs. "Unpublish still goes through the standard confirm dialog"

attacks.claim: The embargo time is shown in the newsroom timezone without a timezone label, so editors outside that zone or reading across days may misread the lift time.
attacks.evidence: formatInNewsroomTz(draft.embargoUntil!, "MMM d, HH:mm") with no timezone abbreviation in the rendered text

attacks.claim: The PR makes contrast and theming claims without any screenshots, contrast measurements, tests, or dark/light verification, which is how the light-theme invisible-text defect got through.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: screenshots, contrast ratios, or test results for light and dark themes
